subtitle.en: The partition of the Mataram Sultanate and the birth of Yogyakarta, 1746–1755
subtitle.id: Pembagian Kerajaan Mataram dan lahirnya Kasultanan Yogyakarta, 1746–1755

description.en: The Third Javanese War of Succession (1746–1757) and the landmark diplomatic treaty that partitioned the Mataram Sultanate (*palihan nagari*). Following Governor-General van Imhoff's humiliation of Prince Mangkubumi over land in Sukawati, Mangkubumi launched an eight-year insurrection against the Dutch East India Company (VOC) and the compliant court in Surakarta. After the destruction of a VOC column at the Bogowonto River in 1751 and a bitter rift between Mangkubumi and Raden Mas Said, VOC Governor Nicolaas Hartingh pursued secret back-channel diplomacy. On 13 February 1755 at Desa Giyanti, the treaty was signed: Mangkubumi became Sultan Hamengkubuwana I of the newly created Kasultanan Ngayogyakarta Hadiningrat, while Pakubuwana III retained the Kasunanan Surakarta Hadiningrat.
description.id: Perang Takhta Jawa Ketiga (1746–1757) dan perjanjian diplomatik bersejarah yang membelah Kesultanan Mataram (*palihan nagari*). Menyusul penghinaan Gubernur Jenderal Van Imhoff terhadap Pangeran Mangkubumi terkait tanah lungguh di Sukawati, Mangkubumi melancarkan perlawanan gerilya selama delapan tahun melawan VOC dan keraton Surakarta. Setelah kehancuran pasukan VOC di Sungai Bogowonto pada 1751 dan perpecahan antara Mangkubumi dengan Raden Mas Said, Gubernur VOC Nicolaas Hartingh menempuh jalur diplomasi rahasia. Pada 13 Februari 1755 di Desa Giyanti, perjanjian ditandatangani: Mangkubumi dinobatkan sebagai Sultan Hamengkubuwana I dari Kasultanan Ngayogyakarta Hadiningrat, sementara Pakubuwana III memimpin Kasunanan Surakarta Hadiningrat.

contentWarning.en: Describes 18th-century warfare, ambushes, decapitations of combatants, dynastic fratricide, and colonial partition.
contentWarning.id: Menggambarkan peperangan abad ke-18, sergapan gerilya, pemenggalan korban tempur, perselisihan keluarga istana, dan pemecahan wilayah oleh kekuasaan kolonial.

description.en: The rebel army of Prince Mangkubumi (later Sultan Hamengkubuwana I), comprising loyal princes, regional bupatis from Sukawati and Grobogan, Islamic clerics, and local levies who rejected VOC dominance.
description.id: Laskar perlawanan Pangeran Mangkubumi (kelak Sultan Hamengkubuwana I), terdiri atas para pangeran setia, bupati daerah Sukawati dan Grobogan, kalangan ulama santri, serta laskar rakyat yang menolak dominasi VOC.

description.en: The fierce, mobile cavalry and infantry guerrillas under Prince Sambernyawa ('Reaper of Souls', later Mangkunegara I). Initially allied with Mangkubumi, he broke away in 1752 and fought all parties until the 1757 Treaty of Salatiga.
description.id: Laskar kavaleri dan infanteri gerilya pimpinan Raden Mas Said ('Pangeran Sambernyawa', kelak Adipati Mangkunegara I). Awalnya bersekutu dengan Mangkubumi, ia memisahkan diri pada 1752 dan bertempur mandiri hingga Perjanjian Salatiga 1757.

description.en: The armed forces and administration of the Dutch East India Company on Java's northeast coast, fielding European troops, naval artillery, and indigenous auxiliaries from Madura, Bugis, and Maluku.
description.id: Kekuatan militer dan administrasi VOC di Pesisir Timur Laut Jawa, mengerahkan serdadu Eropa, artileri laut, serta laskar bantu pribumi dari Madura, Bugis, dan Maluku.

description.en: The royal court of Mataram at Surakarta under Susuhunan Pakubuwana II and subsequently Pakubuwana III, heavily indebted to and diplomatically constrained by the VOC.
description.id: Pemerintahan keraton Mataram di Surakarta di bawah Susuhunan Pakubuwana II dan selanjutnya Pakubuwana III, yang terikat utang politik dan perjanjian protektorat dengan VOC.

notes.en: Keraton Surakarta Hadiningrat, established by Pakubuwana II in 1745 after the sack of Kartasura.
notes.id: Keraton Surakarta Hadiningrat, didirikan oleh Pakubuwana II pada 1745 setelah keruntuhan Kartasura.

notes.en: The ruined capital of the Mataram Empire, abandoned after the Chinese War (Geger Pacinan) of 1742.
notes.id: Bekas ibu kota Kesultanan Mataram yang runtuh dan ditinggalkan akibat Geger Pacinan tahun 1742.

notes.en: Contested apanage land of 3,000 cacah promised to Prince Mangkubumi, triggering his rebellion when cancelled.
notes.id: Tanah lungguh 3.000 cacah yang dijanjikan kepada Pangeran Mangkubumi, memicu perlawanan saat dibatalkan.

notes.en: Headquarters of the VOC Governor of Java's Northeast Coast (Gouvernement van Java's Noordoostkust).

summary.en: VOC Governor-General Van Imhoff publicly insults Prince Mangkubumi at Surakarta and revokes his promised fief in Sukawati, prompting Mangkubumi to leave the court in revolt.
summary.id: Gubernur Jenderal VOC Van Imhoff menghina Pangeran Mangkubumi di Surakarta dan mencabut hak tanah lungguh Sukawati yang dijanjikan, mendorong Mangkubumi angkat senjata.

summary.en: Mangkubumi unites with Raden Mas Said at Sukawati, sealing the rebel alliance with the marriage of his daughter Ratu Bendara to Said.
summary.id: Pangeran Mangkubumi bergabung dengan Raden Mas Said di Sukawati, mempererat persekutuan dengan menikahkan putrinya, Ratu Bendara, kepada Raden Mas Said.

summary.en: On his deathbed, a despairing Sunan Pakubuwana II signs a contract ceding full sovereignty of the Mataram Empire to the Dutch East India Company.
summary.id: Dalam keadaan sakit parah, Sunan Pakubuwana II menandatangani perjanjian penyerahan kedaulatan penuh Kesultanan Mataram kepada VOC.

summary.en: Baron van Hohendorff installs the 17-year-old Raden Mas Suryadi as Susuhunan Pakubuwana III of Surakarta under strict VOC vassalage.
summary.id: Baron van Hohendorff melantik Raden Mas Suryadi yang berusia 17 tahun menjadi Susuhunan Pakubuwana III di Surakarta di bawah naungan protektorat VOC.

summary.en: At Kabanaran in southern Mataram, rebel chiefs, princes, and Muslim clerics acclaim Pangeran Mangkubumi as the rightful Susuhunan of Mataram.
summary.id: Di Kabanaran, para bangsawan perlawanan dan ulama memproklamasikan Pangeran Mangkubumi sebagai Susuhunan Mataram yang sah (Sunan Kabanaran).

summary.en: Mangkubumi ambushes and completely destroys a premier VOC field column at the Bogowonto River. Captain De Clerck is slain, forcing VOC leadership to reconsider military victory.
summary.id: Pasukan Mangkubumi menyergap dan membinasakan kolom ekspedisi VOC di tepi Sungai Bogowonto. Kapten De Clerck tewas, memaksa VOC mengakui ketidakmungkinan menang secara militer.

summary.en: Raden Mas Said demands co-sovereignty and paramount military authority. Mangkubumi refuses, shattering the rebel coalition into rival camps.
summary.id: Raden Mas Said menuntut kekuasaan setara dan otoritas militer tertinggi. Mangkubumi menolak, memecah persekutuan perlawanan menjadi kubu yang saling bersaing.

summary.en: Newly installed VOC Governor Nicolaas Hartingh abandons war in favor of secret negotiations with Mangkubumi through Tumenggung Yudanegara of Banyumas.
summary.id: Gubernur VOC Nicolaas Hartingh yang baru dilantik menghentikan upaya militer dan membuka perundingan rahasia dengan Mangkubumi melalui Bupati Banyumas Tumenggung Yudanegara.

summary.en: Hartingh and Mangkubumi meet in a tent at Pedagangan (Grobogan). Mangkubumi agrees to take the title of Sultan, partition Mataram into two realms, and share court regalia.
summary.id: Hartingh dan Mangkubumi bertemu di tenda perundingan di Pedagangan. Mangkubumi bersedia memakai gelar Sultan, membagi Mataram menjadi dua kerajaan, dan membagi pusaka keraton.

name.en: Signing of the Treaty of Giyanti

summary.en: The historic Treaty of Giyanti is ratified at Desa Giyanti. The Mataram Empire is officially divided: Hamengkubuwana I takes the western half (Yogyakarta), and Pakubuwana III the eastern half (Surakarta).
summary.id: Perjanjian bersejarah Giyanti diratifikasi di Desa Giyanti. Mataram resmi dibelah dua (*palihan nagari*): Hamengkubuwana I memerintah bagian barat (Yogyakarta), dan Pakubuwana III bagian timur (Surakarta).

summary.en: Pakubuwana III and Hamengkubuwana I meet in reconciliation at Jatisari. They divide Javanese royal regalia, court attire, keris styles, gamelan tunes, and classical dance forms.
summary.id: Pakubuwana III dan Hamengkubuwana I bertemu di Jatisari untuk membagi pusaka, gaya busana adat, corak keris, gending gamelan, dan tari keraton antara Surakarta dan Yogyakarta.

summary.en: Sultan Hamengkubuwana I officially proclaims the birth of Kasultanan Ngayogyakarta Hadiningrat, selecting the forest of Beringan as the site of his permanent capital.
summary.id: Sultan Hamengkubuwana I memproklamasikan berdirinya Kasultanan Ngayogyakarta Hadiningrat dan menetapkan Hutan Beringan sebagai lokasi ibu kota istananya.

body.en:
In May 1746, Governor-General Gustaaf Willem van Imhoff arrived at the newly established Keraton Surakarta. The Mataram Empire was exhausted following the Chinese War, and Sunan Pakubuwana II had promised his capable half-brother, Prince Mangkubumi, an apanage fief of 3,000 peasant households in Sukawati (Sragen) for quelling Raden Mas Said's rebellion.

Van Imhoff harshly intervened, demanding the direct lease of Java's north coast and berating Pakubuwana II for his generosity. At the urging of Chief Minister Patih Pringgalaya, the grant was revoked. Publicly humiliated before the assembled court, Prince Mangkubumi quietly walked out of Surakarta on 19 May 1746, rode east to Sukawati, and formed a fighting alliance with his nephew Raden Mas Said.
body.id:
Pada Mei 1746, Gubernur Jenderal Gustaaf Willem van Imhoff tiba di Keraton Surakarta yang baru didirikan. Mataram sedang lunglai usai Geger Pacinan, dan Sunan Pakubuwana II telah menjanjikan tanah lungguh 3.000 cacah di Sukawati (Sragen) kepada adiknya yang cakap, Pangeran Mangkubumi, atas jasanya meredam pemberontakan Raden Mas Said.

Van Imhoff campur tangan secara kasar, menuntut sewa pesisir utara dan mencela Pakubuwana II di depan umum karena terlalu bermurah hati. Atas hasutan Patih Pringgalaya, janji tanah lungguh dibatalkan. Merasa dihina martabatnya di depan para bangsawan, Pangeran Mangkubumi meninggalkan istana pada 19 Mei 1746, bergerak ke timur menuju Sukawati, dan bersumpah angkat senjata bersama keponakannya, Raden Mas Said.

body.en:
By late 1749, Mangkubumi and Raden Mas Said commanded immense popular support across Grobogan, Demak, Madiun, and Sukawati. In Surakarta, Sunan Pakubuwana II fell mortally ill. Fearing the imminent collapse of his dynasty, the dying monarch placed his kingdom into the hands of the VOC. On 11 December 1749, Baron van Hohendorff obtained the Sunan's signature on a treaty transferring the supreme sovereignty of Mataram to the Dutch East India Company.

Four days later, Pakubuwana II died. The VOC crowned his 17-year-old son as Sunan Pakubuwana III in Surakarta. However, three days earlier at his rebel camp in Kabanaran, southern Mataram, Mangkubumi had already been proclaimed legitimate Susuhunan by royal relatives and prominent Islamic clerics, setting up two rival monarchs claiming the Mataram throne.
body.id:
Menjelang akhir 1749, perlawanan Mangkubumi dan Raden Mas Said telah meluas dari Grobogan, Demak, Madiun hingga Sukawati. Di Surakarta, Sunan Pakubuwana II jatuh sakit parah. Dicekam kekhawatiran akan keruntuhan kerajaannya, sang Sunan menyerahkan nasib takhta kepada Kompeni. Pada 11 Desember 1749, Baron van Hohendorff memperoleh tanda tangan perjanjian penyerahan kedaulatan Mataram kepada VOC.

Empat hari berselang, Pakubuwana II wafat. VOC menobatkan putranya yang masih belia sebagai Sunan Pakubuwana III di Surakarta. Namun, tiga hari sebelumnya di perkemahan Kabanaran (selatan Yogyakarta), Pangeran Mangkubumi telah diangkat oleh para pangeran dan ulama sebagai Susuhunan Mataram yang sah (Sunan Kabanaran). Dua matahari kini terbit di langit tanah Jawa.

body.en:
Determined to crush the rebellion once and for all, the VOC mobilized a formidable field force under Captain J.J. de Clerck, reinforced by auxiliary troops and court levies under Patih Pringgalaya. In late October 1751, the Dutch expedition pushed into Bagelen toward the Bogowonto River near Jenar.

Mangkubumi's commander, Tumenggung Suranegara, lured the Dutch column into marshy terrain along the swollen river before springing a devastating ambush. In hours of intense hand-to-hand combat, Mangkubumi's warriors broke the Dutch defensive squares. Captain De Clerck was decapitated on the battlefield, his officers slaughtered, and his artillery captured. The catastrophic defeat convinced the VOC Council in Batavia that Mangkubumi could never be eliminated by military force alone.
body.id:
Bertekad menumpas perlawanan secara tuntas, VOC mengerahkan ekspedisi militer besar di bawah Kapten J.J. de Clerck, diperkuat pasukan bantu dan prajurit keraton pimpinan Patih Pringgalaya. Pada akhir Oktober 1751, pasukan Belanda merangsek ke Bagelen mendekati Sungai Bogowonto di wilayah Jenar.

Panglima Mangkubumi, Tumenggung Suranegara, memancing kolom Belanda ke medan berlumpur di tepi sungai yang meluap sebelum melancarkan sergapan dahsyat. Dalam pertempuran jarak dekat yang sengit, laskar Mangkubumi meremukkan formasi bertahan Belanda. Kapten De Clerck tewas terpenggal di medan tempur, para perwiranya binasa, dan meriam-meriam VOC dirampas. Kehancuran telak ini menyadarkan Batavia bahwa Mangkubumi mustahil ditundukkan dengan kekuatan senjata semata.

body.en:
Despite their military triumphs, discord erupted within the rebel coalition. Raden Mas Said, renowned as Pangeran Sambernyawa ('Reaper of Souls') for his audacious cavalry tactics, grew resentful of playing second fiddle to his uncle. Said demanded equal status as an independent ruler and paramount commander of the armed forces.

In mid-1752 at Kasatriyan near Ponorogo, a heated council ended in complete fracture. Mangkubumi insisted on undivided royal authority. Said withdrew his seasoned veteran fighters, divorced Mangkubumi's daughter Ratu Bendara, and waged a ferocious independent war against the VOC, Surakarta, and Mangkubumi simultaneously. The split fundamentally altered the strategic balance of Java.
body.id:
Di tengah rentetan kemenangan militer, keretakan hebat membayangi kubu perlawanan. Raden Mas Said, yang berjuluk Pangeran Sambernyawa karena keberanian dan ketangkasannya memimpin kavaleri gerilya, menolak terus berada di bawah bayang-bayang pamannya. Said menuntut status sederajat sebagai penguasa berdaulat dan panglima perang tertinggi.

Pada pertengahan 1752 di Kasatriyan dekat Ponorogo, musyawarah berakhir dengan perpecahan total. Mangkubumi mempertahankan prinsip kekuasaan tunggal monarki. Raden Mas Said menarik pasukannya, menceraikan Ratu Bendara (putri Mangkubumi), dan melancarkan perang mandiri melawan VOC, Surakarta, maupun Mangkubumi sekaligus. Perpecahan ini mengubah peta kekuatan secara mendasar di Pulau Jawa.

body.en:
In early 1754, Nicolaas Hartingh assumed office as the VOC Governor of Java's Northeast Coast in Semarang. Fluent in Javanese, deeply attuned to local customs, and pragmatically opposed to endless war expenditures, Hartingh recognized that Mangkubumi was exhausted by war and threatened by Raden Mas Said's rogue forces.

Hartingh initiated secret correspondence through Tumenggung Yudanegara, the Bupati of Banyumas, and a respected Muslim trader named Seh Ibrahim. Messages dispatched through back-channels assured Mangkubumi that the Company was prepared to recognize his royal dignity and territory if he would agree to a lasting partition and peace.
body.id:
Pada awal 1754, Nicolaas Hartingh memangku jabatan Gubernur VOC untuk Pesisir Timur Laut Jawa di Semarang. Menguasai bahasa Jawa secara fasih, memahami adat istiadat setempat, dan enggan memboroskan kas VOC untuk perang berkepanjangan, Hartingh menyadari bahwa Mangkubumi telah letih berperang dan kini terancam oleh laskar liar Raden Mas Said.

Hartingh membuka saluran diplomasi rahasia melalui Bupati Banyumas Tumenggung Yudanegara dan saudagar muslim terpercaya Seh Ibrahim. Surat-menyurat rahasia itu meyakinkan Mangkubumi bahwa Kompeni bersedia mengakui kedaulatannya atas separuh wilayah Mataram asalkan tercipta perdamaian yang abadi.

body.en:
On 22 September 1754, Governor Hartingh and Prince Mangkubumi met face-to-face inside a pavilion tent at Desa Pedagangan in Grobogan. The talks were tense: Mangkubumi initially refused to surrender the title of Susuhunan, pointing to Cirebon as precedent for multiple sultans in one realm, while Hartingh insisted that two Sunans in Mataram would invite perpetual civil war.

The next day, a breakthrough was forged. Mangkubumi agreed to assume the royal title of Sultan rather than Susuhunan. In return, the Mataram realm would be partitioned equally (*palihan nagari*), the VOC would pay annual compensation for coastal leases, and half of the sacred court pusakas would be transferred to Mangkubumi. In November 1754, Sunan Pakubuwana III formally gave his assent from Surakarta.
body.id:
Pada 22 September 1754, Gubernur Hartingh dan Pangeran Mangkubumi bertemu langsung di tenda perundingan Desa Pedagangan, Grobogan. Suasana sempat tegang: Mangkubumi menolak melepas gelar Susuhunan dengan mencontohkan Kesultanan Cirebon yang memiliki lebih dari satu sultan, sedangkan Hartingh menegaskan bahwa dua Sunan di Mataram hanya akan melahirkan perang abadi.

Keesokan harinya, tercapai titik temu. Mangkubumi sepakat memakai gelar Sultan alih-alih Susuhunan. Sebagai imbalan, wilayah Mataram dibagi dua sama rata (*palihan nagari*), VOC membayar kompensasi tahunan atas sewa pesisir, dan separuh pusaka keraton diserahkan kepada Mangkubumi. Pada November 1754, Sunan Pakubuwana III dari Surakarta mengirimkan surat persetujuan resmi.

body.en:
On 13 February 1755 (Kemis Kliwon, 29 Rabingulakir 1680 Anno Javanico), the delegations assembled at Desa Giyanti, southeast of Karanganyar. There, Nicolaas Hartingh as plenipotentiary of the VOC and Prince Mangkubumi signed the Treaty of Giyanti, witnessed by representatives of Sunan Pakubuwana III.

The treaty formally dissolved the unified empire of Mataram. Pakubuwana III retained the eastern half as Kasunanan Surakarta Hadiningrat, while Mangkubumi took the western half under the regal name Sri Sultan Hamengkubuwana I Senapati ing Ngalaga Sayidin Panatagama Kalifatullah.

Two days later, on 15 February 1755 at Jatisari (Lebak), Pakubuwana III and Sultan Hamengkubuwana I met in person. Embracing with tears of reconciliation, they concluded the cultural partition: Surakarta preserved the established court customs, while Yogyakarta adopted the classic Demak-Mataram styles for palace attire, keris sheaths, gamelan compositions, and court dance.
body.id:
Pada 13 Februari 1755 (Kemis Kliwon, 29 Rabingulakir 1680 Tahun Jawa), para delegasi berkumpul di Desa Giyanti, tenggara Karanganyar. Di tempat itu, Nicolaas Hartingh selaku komisioner VOC dan Pangeran Mangkubumi menandatangani naskah Perjanjian Giyanti, disaksikan oleh perwakilan Sunan Pakubuwana III.

Perjanjian ini secara resmi membagi wilayah Kesultanan Mataram (*palihan nagari*). Pakubuwana III memerintah separuh wilayah timur sebagai Kasunanan Surakarta Hadiningrat, sementara Mangkubumi memerintah separuh barat dengan gelar Sri Sultan Hamengkubuwana I Senapati ing Ngalaga Sayidin Panatagama Kalifatullah.

Dua hari berselang, pada 15 Februari 1755 di Jatisari (Lebak), Pakubuwana III dan Sultan Hamengkubuwana I bertemu secara langsung. Dalam pertemuan penuh haru itu, disepakati pembagian budaya: Surakarta mempertahankan tata cara keraton yang ada, sedangkan Yogyakarta melestarikan corak klasik warisan Demak-Mataram dalam hal busana istana, warangka keris, gending gamelan, dan tari bedhaya.

body.en:
On 13 March 1755 (Kemis Pon, 29 Jumadilawal 1680 AJ), Sultan Hamengkubuwana I issued the royal declaration of Hadeging Nagari Ngayogyakarta Hadiningrat. For his permanent capital, he chose the sacred forest of Beringan between the Code and Winongo rivers, a strategic location nestled between Mount Merapi to the north and the Indian Ocean to the south.

Over the following eighteen months, thousands of craftsmen and laborers cleared the forest and constructed the sprawling pavilions, fortifications, mosques, and water palaces of the Kraton. On 7 October 1756 (Kemis Pahing, 13 Sura 1682 AJ), Sultan Hamengkubuwana I and his court processed in grand state into the new Keraton Ngayogyakarta Hadiningrat, establishing the enduring cultural and spiritual capital of Yogyakarta.
body.id:
Pada 13 Maret 1755 (Kemis Pon, 29 Jumadilawal 1680 AJ), Sultan Hamengkubuwana I mengumumkan proklamasi Hadeging Nagari Ngayogyakarta Hadiningrat. Sebagai pusat pemerintahan abadi, Sultan memilih Hutan Beringan di antara Sungai Code dan Sungai Winongo—posisi kosmologis strategis di antara Gunung Merapi di utara dan Laut Selatan.

Selama delapan belas bulan berikutnya, ribuan perajin dan prajurit membabat hutan dan membangun kompleks keraton, benteng baluwarti, masjid agung, dan taman air Tamansari. Pada 7 Oktober 1756 (Kemis Pahing, 13 Sura 1682 AJ), Sultan Hamengkubuwana I bersama keluarga istana secara resmi boyongan memasuki Keraton Ngayogyakarta Hadiningrat, menandai berdirinya pusat peradaban dan kebudayaan Jawa yang lestari hingga hari ini.
